title: Coral and the Archive
premise: Rosalind Coldharbour, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent a decade hauling cargo through contested orbits under a false identity. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, he realizes it was a weapon test—and that the same event erased an entire mining colony from every record. To prove the massacre happened, Rosalind must recover the vault's hidden physical archive, the one place uncorrupted data survives, while the corporation behind the flicker hunts him and his own buried past as the colony's sole survivor unravels. In the end he broadcasts the truth at the cost of his anonymity, choosing to exist publicly rather than survive invisibly.
about_author: Ulyana Montrose is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps a small, obsessively catalogued library of obsolete storage media.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Hauling cargo near the dead seed vault, Rosalind feels gravity stutter for exactly nine seconds; instruments confirm it happened system-wide, yet no feed acknowledges it. The beat is quiet dread—the moment invisibility stops being safe.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He returns to the vault to log the anomaly and finds his own maintenance records subtly altered—shifted dates, a missing week ten years ago. Emotional beat: unease curdling into suspicion about his own curated history.

chapters.title: Cargo for Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A routine delivery to station Meridian reveals the colony of Kestrel's Landing simply doesn't exist in any registry—yet Rosalind's muscle memory knows its docking codes. Beat: vertigo of gaslighting.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vann, a disgraced archivist, contacts Rosalind claiming she also felt the flicker and remembers Kestrel's Landing. Their wary alliance forms over contraband paper records. Beat: fragile hope of not being alone.

chapters.title: Orbital Traffic
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Corporate patrol ships begin shadowing his route; a 'customs inspection' nearly exposes his forged identity. He realizes someone flagged him the moment the gravity flickered. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Know
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Inside the vault's deep stacks, he discovers the seed inventory conceals a second archive—an analog, air-gapped record vault built by the original founders. Beat: first real leverage.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She admits she once worked for Halcyon Dynamics' memory-integrity division and helped design the record-erasure protocol. Beat: guilt, and Rosalind's trust cracking.

chapters.title: The Nine-Second Weapon
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Decrypted fragments reveal the flicker was a field test of a gravity-lance array—and Kestrel's Landing was the target. Beat: cold fury replacing fear.

chapters.title: Ghost Codes
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. His knowledge of Kestrel's docking codes deepens: fragments of childhood surface—a mother's voice, a red door. He begins suspecting he lived there. Beat: identity trembling.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Smugglers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He trades favors with orbit-smuggler crew the Ferrous Daughters to move the analog archive off-world. Beat: uneasy camaraderie, the cost of allies.

chapters.title: Halcyon Comes Calling
chapters.summary: POV Director Osei Sable, Halcyon's security chief. We see the hunt from the predator's side: Sable orders Rosalind's history rewritten further, revealing how casually power edits people. Beat: chilling institutional banality.

chapters.title: The Missing Week
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Following the altered ledger, Rosalind finds his own cryo-stasis pod in a derelict medbay—he was wiped and re-seeded after Kestrel fell. Beat: grief for a self he can't retrieve.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. A Meridian contact sells them out; Ilsa is captured buying time for Rosalind to escape with the archive core. Beat: sacrifice and self-loathing.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Silent-running through debris fields, pursued by Sable's ships, Rosalind confronts that survival has always been his only skill—and asks what it's for. Beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Founders' Intent
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The analog archive includes founders' testimony: the vault was built precisely because corporations would one day edit reality. Beat: inheritance—he is the vault's true last line.

chapters.title: Rescue Attempt
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind with Ferrous Daughters. A raid on Halcyon's holding station to free Ilsa goes half-wrong: she's freed but the Daughters lose a ship and a friend. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind/Sable. Captured briefly, Rosalind is offered restoration of his full memories in exchange for silence. Beat: temptation—he could be whole again if he agrees to stay a lie.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Chooses
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He refuses, escaping during transfer, but Sable now knows the archive's location and moves to burn the vault itself. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Burning Stacks
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Halcyon torpedoes the vault's upper levels; Rosalind races through fire to reach the analog core as centuries of seeds burn around him. Beat: climax begins—desperate, sacrificial.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Using the vault's ancient transmitter array, he beams the massacre records on every open channel, unencrypted, untraceable, unerasable—exposing himself completely. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The broadcast ignites system-wide inquiry; Sable is arrested by her own board, which sacrifices her to survive. Ilsa testifies, finding redemption in public truth. Beat: justice, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Coral and the Archive
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Among the scorched vault, one seed chamber survived; Rosalind, no longer hiding, plants it and takes his real name back—Kestrel Coldharbour. Beat: quiet resolution—identity reclaimed, survival redefined as living visibly.
